label: F-f91643

findings.note: Plan §12 item 7 (todo/PLAN…md:846 at 407442b5) admits the stories 2–4 code came before their tests, but the reds were then seen by stubbing out the behaviour the tests depend on, which is the 'prove the test has teeth' route in common/testing.md:329; the lapse is real and was disclosed, so calling it blocking overstates it.

At 407442b5 the diff adds a ProviderStatus.Cooldown wire member read by src_vs_code (ServerJsonContext.cs:58-68) but leaves research/architecture.md untouched, which breaks knowledge-base.md:25; the next commit 4a045a85 fixed it.
The plan's D1/D2 (plan :188, :699) chose a three-valued bool? Spent explicitly and passed the plan gate, so asking for a different type goes against a plan decision.

A torn or unparseable file being overwritten whole by the next park is the plan's own decision (§8, plan :655-656); QuotaCooldowns.cs:236 deliberately lets only I/O errors propagate under the lock, which is the case where real entries could be lost.

QuotaCooldowns.cs:265-269 does probe one key at a time, but only agy keys run a child process (about 3 in practice, not 6), the plan accepts a 30 s bound per key (§8 :661), and the round's token cancels the probes.

The 16 KiB in the plan is a budget on what the writer produces (S20), not a read guard; MostBytes at QuotaCooldowns.cs:57 is only a sanity ceiling, and rejecting a valid file at 16 KiB would make it unreadable and get it overwritten.

The plan requires HeldFile.TakeWithin, the product's one cross-process lock (D4 :251), and QuotaCooldowns.cs:287-288 already moves that blocking spin off the async continuation with Task.Run, on purpose.
The plan's D5/D6 (plan :272, :292-296) puts ReadResetAsync on IReviewerRuntime and has it take IProcessLauncher; a separate probe abstraction is a matter of taste that goes against the plan.
Gate F1 (plan :246-248, :787) decided against a new registration because ProvidersAnswer's graph already reaches CooldownReport, and S38 serialises one through the context.

PanelService.cs:498 ranks an unavailable sign-in above a cooldown on purpose: that row cannot run whatever its quota says, so naming the auth cure is the right sentence, and the finding's account of the ordering is muddled.

The only wait in Apply is the lock wait, which the plan bounds at 30 s and accepts (§8 :657); the probes do take the round's token (QuotaCooldowns.cs:269), and a Task.Run token only affects scheduling anyway.
This repeats index 3: plan §8 :656 says a torn file 'is overwritten whole by the next park', and the 'never overwritten blindly' text the finding quotes is not in the DoD (plan :620-621).

D4 (plan :229-230) specifies the note as this side's sentence followed by the vendor's sentence redacted through VendorReason.Written and capped at 400 characters, which is exactly what QuotaCooldowns.cs:318, 191 and 332 do.
D4 (plan :232-233) says 'read on every CanRun, no cache' on purpose, so a park written by another process is seen at once and the file stays under 16 KiB.
This duplicates index 4: QuotaCooldowns.cs:265-269 runs the probes one after another, but the plan accepts a 30 s bound per agy key, and only agy keys launch a process.
The plan (DoD :633) asks for the time left rounded up, and QuotaWords.cs:24-28 rounds up so it never claims a quota is back too early; the hours-to-minutes step is a matter of taste.

summary: Only the missing architecture.md update is a clear, useful defect (the team fixed it in the next commit); the red-first lapse and the sequential probes are real points but overstated. Most other findings ask for things the plan explicitly decided against, such as no cache, overwriting a torn file, the bool? Spent verdict, no new JSON registration and the probe living in the runtime adapter, or misread intended behaviour, so most of this review is noise.
